question: What primary hormonal shift triggers the physiological changes of menopause?

options.A: A sudden surge in active progesterone levels
options.B: Total cessation of thyroid hormone secretion
options.C: Declining ovarian function and oestrogen production
options.D: Permanent overactivity of the adrenal glands

explanation: Menopause happens naturally when the ovaries gradually slow down and produce much lower levels of oestrogen and progesterone. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why are lifestyle modifications considered the foundation of menopausal management?

options.A: They guarantee complete immunity against chronic midlife illnesses
options.B: They safely support overall health and ease symptoms for every woman
options.C: They completely replace the need for any clinical assessments
options.D: They stop the natural ageing process of the reproductive organs

explanation: Every woman goes through midlife hormonal changes, and lifestyle habits directly influence how severe her symptoms and long-term health risks will be. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h1)

question: Name ONE common food source that is rich in natural phytoestrogens.
explanation: Legumes, especially soybeans, contain plant compounds called phytoestrogens that weakly interact with oestrogen receptors in the body. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is increasing dietary calcium and Vitamin D especially important for menopausal women?

options.A: To help combat accelerated bone mineral density loss
options.B: To prevent sudden spikes in daily blood pressure
options.C: To completely eliminate mild daytime hot flushes
options.D: To speed up sluggish thyroid hormone production

explanation: Lower oestrogen levels after menopause speed up bone breakdown, making adequate calcium and Vitamin D vital to prevent osteoporosis. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which type of exercise directly stimulates bone formation and preserves muscle mass in midlife?
explanation: Working muscles against resistance places a healthy physical stress on bones, which triggers them to stay dense and strong. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h3)

question: A 50-year-old woman complains of gradual weight gain and low energy. What is the best initial exercise advice to give her?

options.A: Undergo immediate high-intensity physical training every single day
options.B: Avoid all forms of physical activity until her hormones stabilise
options.C: Combine regular brisk walking with simple resistance training sessions
options.D: Engage exclusively in heavy weightlifting without any aerobic exercise

explanation: A balanced routine of aerobic activity for the heart and resistance training for muscles and bones safely addresses both weight and energy concerns. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which substance should women experiencing menopausal insomnia avoid close to bedtime?
explanation: Caffeine is a central nervous system stimulant, and alcohol causes frequent night waking, both of which ruin healthy sleep patterns. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h4)

question: How does keeping the bedroom cool directly help a menopausal woman sleep better?

options.A: It forces the body to enter deep REM sleep instantly
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying hormonal imbalances
options.C: It helps reduce the severity and impact of night sweats
options.D: It stops the production of melatonin in the brain

explanation: A cool environment helps regulate body temperature, preventing sudden temperature spikes from waking the woman up. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h4)

question: What hormone is released in higher amounts during periods of chronic psychological stress?
explanation: Cortisol is the primary stress hormone produced by the adrenal glands when the body perceives prolonged pressure or tension. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is it clinically important for midwives to address the emotional and psychological aspects of menopause?

options.A: Emotional symptoms mean the reproductive organs are diseased
options.B: Counseling is the only legal treatment permitted for midwives
options.C: Psychological stress has no actual effect on the endocrine system
options.D: Mental well-being is deeply connected to physical symptom severity

explanation: Stress and anxiety amplify how a woman feels physical changes like hot flushes, making mental health care an essential part of management. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which harmful habit accelerates both vascular damage and bone mineral loss in menopausal women?
explanation: Smoking harms blood vessels and lowers active oestrogen levels in the body, which speeds up both heart disease and osteoporosis. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following changes in lipid profiles commonly occurs after the loss of oestrogen?

options.A: An increase in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol
options.B: A massive drop in total blood glucose levels
options.C: A permanent surge in beneficial HDL cholesterol

explanation: Oestrogen helps protect the heart by keeping cholesterol levels healthy; when it drops, harmful LDL cholesterol tends to rise. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is a personalised approach better than a rigid rule list when counseling women on lifestyle changes?

options.A: It ensures the woman takes expensive medications every single day
options.B: It respects the patient's individual reality and builds lasting habits
options.C: It guarantees that all menopausal symptoms will disappear in a week
options.D: It stops the midwife from having to explain complex medical terms

explanation: Women are much more likely to stick with lifestyle changes when the plan fits their unique lifestyle, culture, and personal goals. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h7)

question: A patient is overwhelmed by advice to change her diet, start exercising, and quit smoking all at once. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Insist she masters all the lifestyle changes before leaving the clinic
options.B: Help her pick one small, manageable change to start with today
options.C: Tell her lifestyle changes are useless and prescribe strong drugs
options.D: Discontinue counseling since she is not ready to follow instructions

explanation: Breaking down lifestyle goals into small, achievable steps prevents overwhelm and encourages long-term success. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h7)
